title: Abba Guria
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Mishnah Kiddushin 4:14: Abba Gurion of Tzaidan says in the name of Abba Guria: A person should not teach his son to be a donkey-driver, potter, sailor, shepherd, or shopkeeper, for their trades are the trades of robbers. R’ Yehudah says in his name (that is, in Abba Guria’s name, according to the Rashi gloss cited by Hyman): Most of the date-dealers are wicked, etc. [The supplied text has “date-dealers”; Hyman’s print has “donkey-drivers.”] Hyman reports that the Jerusalem Talmud there reads: Abba Gurion of Tzaidan says in the name of Abba Shaul.

notes.text: The supplied text says “potter” and “date-dealers.” The checked Mishnah instead lists camel-driver and barber, and later says “donkey-drivers.” These source differences are retained; the Hebrew is not silently emended.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman supplies potter and date-dealers; the earlier recorded Mishnah comparison instead has camel-driver/barber and donkey-drivers. These differences are preserved rather than silently repaired. The Rashi parenthesis is Hyman’s attribution, not a newly inspected commentary. Abba Gurion, Guria and the reported Jerusalem Talmud Abba Shaul reading are distinct transmitted forms. The trade warning and most qualification are preserved; the abbreviated Yehudah title remains R’.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 301) has קדר, “potter,” among the trades and החמרין, “donkey-drivers,” in R’ Yehudah’s statement about most of them. The supplied Hebrew in the latter clause reads התמרין, translated above as “date-dealers.” The Torat Emet Mishnah lists camel-driver and barber, and the Davidson Bavli at Kiddushin 82a lists camel-driver and potter. Rashi there explicitly explains “in his name” as Abba Guria’s. The Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud at Kiddushin 4:11 names Abba Shaul, lists both a barber and a potter, and gives donkey-drivers in R’ Yehudah’s remark.
